With how many Humans you killed, I’m surprised you didn’t get the ending that triggers once you’ve massacred a large number of Human guests. Your fortune will arrive on your doorstep. 

When the intruder questions if you’re home alone, pick the option that states you are home alone. Or, when he returns let him inside. He’s also the one you see standing outside of your window holding the soldier’s head. 

Complete all of egghead’s quests and heed to his further instructions. Fail one of the vigilante’s test. Try being a little more cooperative with FEMA and continue to meet new guests. In total, there are 10 endings, so there’s still plenty more to do; this game is an absolute gem.

SPOILER WARNING ⚠️ 


1.	Yes, I’m Alone (worst)
	•	Let the Super Imposter into the house (either tell him “you’re alone” when he asks, or have no tenants in the house when he shows up). He breaks in and takes you — instant Alone ending.  ￼
	2.	No, I’m not Alone (bad)
	•	Make sure at least one Visitor is in the house when you board up the windows (i.e., don’t purge everyone). When the group turns on you, you’re taken — basement/group ending.  ￼
	3.	Yes, I’m a Murderer (bad)
	•	Reach around day 12 and kill every tenant (even humans). After slaughtering them all you’ll get this ending — paranoia eats the protagonist.  ￼
	4.	Wrath of the Vigilante (bad)
	•	Fail the Vigilante’s test (on his 2nd/3rd visit). Pick any failing test option — Teeth, Armpit, or Photo — you get shot, go mad, and this ending triggers.  ￼
	5.	Shroom or Doom (bad / mushroom route)
	•	Requirements (summary): beat the game once → on night 6 meet the Mushroom Man and take his Book of Smiles page → on day 7 pick the basement mushroom (unlock basement by letting Cat Lady in on night 4) → eat the mushroom → follow the chain (apple on day 8, click bedroom clock day 9, speak to mushroom man at night) → follow him into Mushroom Land on night 10.  ￼
	6.	May Death Cleanse us of Our Sins! (cult ending, ok)
	•	Let the cult leader and his three followers into your house and keep all three alive (avoid FEMA taking any of them; place other guests so cultists keep their seats). When the leader returns, accept his invitation — join the cult.  ￼
	7.	Embrace the Inevitable (ok — dig/tunnel route)
	•	This is multi-step and the most fiddly:
	1.	Watch TV to get the ForRest number; order 2 EnerJeka cans.
	2.	Let Cat Lady in so basement unlocks.
	3.	Reach night 9 and talk to the Prophet.
	4.	Dig in the basement on days 10, 11 and 12; show the Vigilante your eyes (night 10) and hands (night 12).
	5.	Drink an EnerJeka on day 12, use the bathroom mirror prompts, enter the tunnels, turn right to talk to the miner, then jump into the hole he found. This unlocks the burial/tunnel ending.  ￼
	8.	Child of Doom (weird / rare)
	•	A very rare chain: keep a mysterious woman (possibly linked to the protagonist’s past) in your bed, spare her if tested, she appears pregnant at night and dies after childbirth. Then you must find the baby in the house (click several specific environmental spots: right bedroom curtain, ceiling fan in office, bowl under bathtub, then look out the window the same night) — find the baby four times and look out every window that night to trigger this ending.  ￼
	9.	Welcome to FEMA (good)
	•	Be proactive and cooperative with FEMA: use the FEMA hotline when you learn signs, hand out FEMA Notices strategically, and take out at least one Visitor per day (or otherwise make sure FEMA notices you). Cooperate with FEMA officers and you’ll be offered a job — that’s this ending.  ￼
	10.	The End? (best / “survive” ending)

	•	The hardest: reach day 14 with only humans as your tenants. Strategy: use FEMA Notices smartly to remove suspected Visitors, keep reliably human guests alive (recommended: little girl, widowed women who carries her husband around, burnt fireman, tall man), avoid killing humans, and shield your human tenants across FEMA removals (FEMA appears on set nights). If you board up the house on day 14 with only humans inside, you get the best ending.  ￼

comments.text: Tips for this game if you want to read! tw: this is a long comment: 1. Symptoms Aren't Always the Answer: The daily news broadcast will alert you to new visitor symptoms, but you can't rely on them 100%. Humans can sometimes display false "symptoms" (like bloodshot eyes from crying or dirt under fingernails), and Visitors can be very good at hiding them.    2. Look for Multiple Signs: Never trust a single sign. Only take action (like using a FEMA notice or the gun) when you've confirmed multiple signs from different tests, or if a guest's backstory/behavior is highly suspicious.    3. Behavior Matters: Pay close attention to what your guests say and how they act. Discrepancies in their stories, unusual calm, or quick attempts to leave after you've tested them can be more telling than a single physical symptom.            4 Use FEMA Notices Strategically: FEMA notices are a powerful tool. You generally want to use them on a Visitor you are unsure about, as sending a Visitor to FEMA can spare a Human from being taken, and vice-versa. Some less-hostile Visitors can even be kept around as a sacrifice to FEMA to protect your human guests.   5. "Always" Visitors/Humans: Be aware that some characters are preset to either always be a Visitor or always be Human across most playthroughs. While symptoms are random, some character types are a reliable clue (though you may want to avoid searching online for a definitive list on your first few runs to preserve the mystery).    6. Watch the TV: The TV is a great source of new information. The daily broadcast gives you a new symptom, but you can usually click on the TV an extra one or two times each day to find new information, like new items at ForRest (the delivery service) or new phone numbers.   7. Use ForRest (The Delivery Service): Order items like EnerJeka cans often. These restore your stamina, which is crucial for interacting with the environment (testing guests, digging, etc.). Order two at a time when you can.  8. Don't Run Out of People: There are certain nights (like the 3rd, 5th, 9th, and 11th) when the Pale Man visitor appears. If you are alone in your house on these nights, it's an immediate game over. Always ensure you have at least one guest in the house before these nights, even if they are a slight risk.  9. Save Wisely: Your ability to save is limited, usually tied to using a specific item. Save after a big decision or a clear-out to protect your progress, but don't waste the opportunity on a minor action.  10. Check Your Own Symptoms: Use the bathroom mirror to check your own symptoms. You can have a fungal armpit, for example, which you can clean up. This is vital because the Vigilante appears on specific nights (like the 8th, 10th, and 12th) and will demand proof you are not a Visitor—and a dirty armpit is a sign!
